utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll following the same procedure as yesterday. That is, we'll first move into closed session. No preliminaries were announced. While we are ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For the public, just to know, that we'll first spent at least half an hour in private session, up to a half an hour, and that there is a chance that we'll then continue in private session or in -- even in closed session, but there's also a chance that we'll be in open session, but still a possibility of having some protective measures which makes it not easy to follow the proceedings from the public gallery. We turn into closed session in order to allow for the witness to enter the courtroom. And while we are moving into closed session - I'll not dare yet - I just briefly announce that yesterday I signed an order to redact the public transcript. The content was accurate. What was not accurate was a date appearing in this decision. It said the hearing of the 24th of September, 2012. This day I issued a corrected public order giving the right date.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber has decided that it grants the request for protective measures; reasons to follow. Which means, Witness, that your face will not be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- will not be visible on the screens, you are covered by a shield so that even from the public gallery no one can see your face, your voice will be scrambled in the audio, and we'll not use your own name. Now please keep in mind that whenever a question is put to you where the answer could reveal your identity, don't hesitate to ask us to go into private session which would mean that even your answer would not be available to the public outside this courtroom. I also urge the parties to be very precise in asking to go into private session if there's any need to do so. Witness, we'll now proceed to the substance of your testimony. Mr. Jeremy will examine you. Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please see 65 ter 32660 in e-court. Not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, without reading aloud any of the information that you see on the screen before you, does this accurately reflect your name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 32660, under seal, as the next Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7419 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall providing a written statement to the Office of the Prosecutor dated the 1st of July, 2014?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 31080, not to be broadcast, and this the statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, directing your attention to the English version of the document on the right hand of the screen, do you recognise the signature above the signature line on the first page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Can we please go to e-court page 5 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, again, do you recognise your signature above the dotted line on this page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, you should switch off your microphone when the witness is answering.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, have you had an opportunity to read and review this statement in preparation for your appearance here today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And I understand that you wish to clarify and correct certain parts of your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, having now made the corrections to the statement that you have just made, if I were today to ask you similar questions to those that you were asked in the taking of your statement, would you provide the same answers, in substance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the truthfulness and the accuracy of this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 31080 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7420 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, P7420 is admitted into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I now propose to provide a very brief summary of the witness's evidence. I've explained to the witness that the summary is for the public and is not itself part of the evidence, and I've confirmed with the witness that the content of this public summary will not give rise to any security concerns for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, as you suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: RM382 gives evidence about the creation of the Tomasica mass grave and burials in the Tomasica mass grave. Your Honours, that concludes the public summary, and with your leave, I do have some additional questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please put those questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue to hear the evidence of the present witness, the Chamber would like to deliver a decision, a decision on a request that was made yesterday by the Defence. The Chamber denies the request to allocate to the Defence additional time to prepare for the cross-examination of expert witnesses in relation to the Prosecution's reopening case and reasons will follow in due course in writing. That is our decision, and we thought we should inform the parties about it without delay. Then we turn into closed session in order to allow the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Witness, let's look at paragraph 7 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just out of abundance of caution, perhaps it's worth just reminding the witness that we're now in public session, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll do so. Witness, we're now in open session. Still no one can see your face, still no one can hear your voice. But if any answer would tend to reveal your identity, please address me and ask for private session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [No interpretation]. I hope that this is not broadcasted. This statement should not be broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's under seal and it's not broadcasted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Towards the end of the first line on the top you say that: "There were perhaps five civilians there and they were together with Radisa Ljesnjak, a supervisor in charge of the drainage system at Tomasica mine. I do not know why these civilians and Ljesnjak were there. I had the impression that Ljesnjak had connections to the Crisis Staff." I'd like to show you a document that we received recently from the Prosecution. It's a 65 ter. The number is 31037.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for that document to come up on our screens, when you said that you had the impression that Ljesnjak had connections to the Crisis Staff, are you still referring to the Crisis Staff of the mine or are you referring to any other Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Crisis Staff of the mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Witness, in front of us is a document dated the 23rd of February, 1993, where we see that between the 4th of April, 1992, and the 28th of February, 1993, he was a member of the police. He demonstrated exceptional results while carrying out sanitation and hygiene measures at different facilities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. What is the point of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: The Prosecution sent us a proofing note from the other day where you said to them that you didn't know that Mr. Ljesnjak was a member of the police force.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you switch off your microphone when the witness is answering your question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To private session and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We redact this part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see what is recorded. Nothing yet. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. By mistake, a few decisions were given in private session, decisions in the -- on the admission of certain documents. P7425 was admitted under seal; P7426; P7427; P7428; and P7429 were admitted into evidence as public documents -- oh, provisionally under seal. The last four ones provisionally under seal. Apologies for the mistake. We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, I take it that the Prosecution will be ready to call its next witness, which is an expert witness. We resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 24th of June, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of June, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.16 p.m.,
